title: Digital Payment Adoption and Convergence Patterns in Selected Eurasian Economies
content: Digital payment participation captures a distinct dimension of financial service use, although cross-country comparisons are complicated by differences in survey measurement and the bounded nature of adoption. This study examines four Global Findex rounds for 14 purposively selected Eurasian economies, using Kazakhstan as the principal comparative benchmark. Ukraine is excluded from the primary analysis because its abbreviated 2024 questionnaire employed an alternative operationalisation; the original 15-economy sample is retained for sensitivity analysis. Drawing on unrounded estimates and documented survey reference years, the analysis assesses cross-economy dispersion, rank persistence and progress relative to baseline headroom. Mean adoption increased from 34.10% in 2014 to 64.26% in 2024. The cross-economy standard deviation declined from 20.56 to 16.12 percentage points, although the trajectory was non-monotonic. Initial adoption was negatively correlated with absolute gains (r = −0.622), whereas its correlation with headroom-adjusted gains was positive (r = 0.234). The endpoint rank correlation was 0.736. Kazakhstan's adoption rate increased from 46.74% to 85.02%, moving the country from fifth to second place. These findings indicate broader digital payment participation and narrower endpoint dispersion, but show that interpretations of catching-up depend on how progress is measured. For Kazakhstan, the results establish a comparative benchmark for payment participation without identifying causal effects on financial-sector competitiveness.
